clue.text: Novel from which even hot cauldron erupts

indicators.note: erupts suggests the letters of the cauldron's contents spewing out and landing in a new order

parts.note: the fifteen letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A novel in which a pot of steaming liquid boils over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupts' rearranges EVEN HOT CAULDRON; the eruption also fits the title, a 1947 novel by Malcolm Lowry.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm Lowry's celebrated 1947 book is a work of fiction, so a novel is a fair definition.

clue.text: Novel still caging awful brute, having detailed bird

indicators.note: caging means one piece holds the rest inside it, like a bird in a cage

parts.note: still air or water is flat, without movement

indicators.note: awful signals that the word brute is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: the five letters of brute are the fodder

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed: the bird loses its last letter

parts.note: a sparrow is a small common bird

explanation.surface: A novel that keeps a dreadful beast while also describing a bird in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns BRUTE into UBERT; 'detailed' cuts the W from SPARROW; FLAT 'caging' UBERT and SPARRO gives the title of Julian Barnes's 1984 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Barnes's 1984 book about a writer's stuffed bird is a work of fiction.

clue.text: Ben overlooks such a presence as block overlooked, say

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to block or thwart it

indicators.note: say signals that a word spoken gives the letters of a different spelling

parts.note: overlooked means missed, which is pronounced the same as the drizzle word

explanation.surface: A Scottish mountain looms over a ghostly presence, like a block that went unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: A ben is a Scottish mountain, and a Scotch mist is the fine drizzle hanging round it; the phrase also means something imaginary, hence 'presence'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish peak looks down on the thick wet mist that settles over Highland hills, a vague insubstantial presence.

clue.text: Top party affected suavity

indicators.note: Top used as a verb means cut off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a function is a formal party or social gathering

explanation.surface: Someone at a smart party puts on airs of polished charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective for a grand party, but it is the instruction to behead FUNCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction in its figurative sense is an oily, insincere show of earnestness or charm, an affected smoothness.

clue.text: Lethal avalanche's passage from 1

indicators.note: a passage is a stretch of text, here the letters running across the words Lethal avalanche's

explanation.surface: A deadly avalanche makes its way down from a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to the 1-down answer, so the definition reads as what comes out of a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock is the material that pours out of an erupting volcano, the subject of the referenced entry.

clue.text: Novel offering idle talk and desperate message, each after portentous time in conflict

indicators.note: after places the following pieces later in the answer than the time-in-conflict piece
in means the time word sits inside the conflict word

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
the Ides of March were famously foretold as ominous for Julius Caesar
gas is informal for idle chatter
SOS is the distress signal sent in desperation

explanation.surface: A novel full of gossip and a cry for help, set against an ominous moment during a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'after' are the placing words; 'each' supplies its usual abbreviation. The Ides of March were foretold to Caesar, hence portentous. Jean Rhys's 1966 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Rhys's 1966 prequel to Jane Eyre is a work of fiction, so a novel is the definition.

clue.text: Novel speculates about sensual excitement, love finally abandoned

indicators.note: about means the speculation word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to speculate is to theorise

indicators.note: excitement stirs up the letters of sensual into a new order, minus one letter
abandoned means the letter from love is dropped from the stirred-up letters of sensual

parts.note: the seven letters of sensual are the fodder

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word love

explanation.surface: A novel muses on erotic arousal, with romance in the end given up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitement' rearranges SENSUAL; 'abandoned' drops the E that 'love finally' gives, leaving SUNALS; THEORISES goes 'about' that. Hemingway's 1926 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's 1926 debut about expatriates in Paris and Pamplona is a work of fiction.

clue.text: English church with something candid, we hear, lacking English bearing

indicators.note: lacking means the following letter is missing from the plant

parts.note: candid sounds like candied, and angelica stalks are candied for cake decoration
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A church in England is linked with some frank remark, but has lost its English character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Candid' sounds like 'candied': candied angelica is a cake decoration. 'lacking' takes E (English) out of ANGELICA, and the N bearing goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Church of England is the Anglican church, so the adjective describes that English denomination.

clue.text: A match that's brilliant

parts.note: a match is used to give a light

explanation.surface: Striking a match that flares up brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire or lit up shines, so blazing brightly is a sense of brilliant.

clue.text: Fixture's ultimately to provide it

indicators.note: to provide it says these words themselves supply the answer, running across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: What a sports match is ultimately there to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'Fixture's ultimately'; the whole clue also defines it, since a fixture, a scheduled match in British sport, ends in one.
explanation.definitionFit: The final score or outcome is what every scheduled game ends up delivering.

clue.text: Ben taking drug gets cross

parts.note: Ben Travers was an English writer of stage farces
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man named Ben who takes drugs becomes angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' looks like a Scottish mountain or any man; it is Ben Travers, the playwright of the Aldwych farces.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse a stretch of land or water is to go across it from side to side.

clue.text: Small, yet troublesome, irritation

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the letters of yet are unruly and out of order

explanation.surface: A minor but bothersome annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is a small, sore infection that irritates the eye.

clue.text: Laugh at end of tune by Mary Poppins, folk singing

parts.note: a hoot is a burst of laughter

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word tune

parts.note: Mary Poppins is the most famous fictional nanny

explanation.surface: A giggle at the close of a song from Mary Poppins.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Poppins is the magical nanny of P. L. Travers's books and the Disney film.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal gathering for folk music and singing, especially in the US, is known by this word.

clue.text: Test foreign students about student taken in by awful pun

indicators.note: about means the foreign students go around the remaining letters

parts.note: eleves is French for pupils

indicators.note: taken in by means the student letter is held inside the jumbled pun
awful signals the letters of pun are mangled into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: Overseas pupils are examined on a student caught up in a terrible play on words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' gives NPU; L is 'taken in by' it, making NPLU; ELEVES goes 'about' that. The eleven-plus was the English exam deciding grammar-school places at age eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: This examination taken at eleven sorted English children between grammar and secondary modern schools.

clue.text: Old teacher clutching tin, drunk, given free spirit

indicators.note: clutching means the teacher holds the other letters inside

parts.note: beak is old schoolboy slang for a schoolmaster

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of tin are reeling about

explanation.surface: An elderly schoolmaster, can in hand and intoxicated, is a liberated soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' turns TIN into ATNI, which BEAK is 'clutching'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the 1950s Beat Generation rejected convention, an unconventional bohemian free spirit.

clue.text: Feature of garden thus in brief design

indicators.note: in means the thus word sits inside the shortened design
brief means the design word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a plan is a design
ergo is Latin for therefore, thus

explanation.surface: A garden structure included in a short landscape plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts PLAN to PLA, and ERGO goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arched framework of trellis for climbing plants is a typical structure in a garden.

clue.text: Lines may be opposite

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, reversed or contrary in order

explanation.definitionFit: Lines of poetry are set in metre, and the single word also means reversed or contrary.

clue.text: Skill demonstrated by many from start, catching favourite

indicators.note: catching means the shortened start word holds the favourite inside
from means the many letter is taken out of the start word

parts.note: to commence is to start
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Ability shown by many people from the outset, including a favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes M (many) from COMMENCE, leaving COMENCE, which is 'catching' PET.
explanation.definitionFit: Competence is the ability to do something well, a synonym of skill.

clue.text: Prove point with question

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
how is a question word

explanation.surface: Demonstrate a point by asking something.
explanation.definitionFit: To show that something is true is to demonstrate or prove it.

clue.text: Winter accessory, one given hood

parts.note: a scarf is worn round the neck in winter
an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A winter accessory paired with a hood, like a scarf and a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hood' looks like headgear in a clothing scene; it is a hoodlum, Al Capone's nickname, and the gangster film.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone, the most famous gangster or hoodlum, was nicknamed after the scar on his face.

clue.text: Tree, one providing great service?

definitions.meaning: a tennis serve the receiver cannot touch, playfully read as a person who serves superbly

explanation.definitionFit: The botanical name for maples, and also a tennis player who sends down unreturnable serves.

clue.text: Return for attack

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a fit is a sudden attack of illness or temper

explanation.surface: Coming back to make an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A return on an investment is the gain or financial yield it brings.

clue.text: In confines of space, weightless? Drift off

indicators.note: In means the weightless phrase sits inside the outer letters
confines are the boundaries, so the first and last letters of space

parts.note: weightless is read as no oz, no ounces

explanation.surface: An astronaut floating weightless in the bounds of space starts to nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confines of' gives S and E, the first and last letters of 'space'; oz is the abbreviation for ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off into a light sleep is to drift off, as in a short nap.

clue.text: Picture, framing one with many subjects almost good, cleaner

indicators.note: framing means the picture word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to picture something is to see it in the mind

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the monarch is lost

parts.note: a queen rules over many subjects

explanation.surface: A portrait framing a monarch looks nearly good and clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one with many subjects' is a monarch, not a picture's subject matter; 'almost' drops its final letter, and 'framing' wraps the picture word round it and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber-bladed tool for wiping water off windows is a window cleaner's implement.
